A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRC watermarking work. All 26 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Stable Diffusion experiments measuring quality, detectability, robustness and message recovery, plus a CelebA VAE demonstration in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices A and D, including quantitative comparisons and generated-image examples.

M1.justification: PRC-based latent sampling, diffusion inversion, soft-decision detection and belief-propagation decoding are unchanged. The procedures in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–8 remain the same.

E1.justification: Both versions use MS-COCO, Stable Diffusion Prompts, PromptHero prompts for variability evaluation, and CelebA for the VAE demonstration. The watermark removal, spoofing and message-recovery scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Both evaluate DwtDct, DwtDctSvd, RivaGAN, StegaStamp, SSL, Stable Signature, Tree-Ring and Gaussian Shading. Comparator membership also remains unchanged within the variability, classifier and attack comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain Stable Diffusion 2.1, 512×512 images, guidance scale 3.0, 50 sampling and inversion steps, and TPR@FPR=0.01. Sample counts and appendix attack settings are unchanged; the JPEG settings merely move from page 15 to page 19.

E4.justification: The sparsity comparison, detectability tests, removal and spoofing attacks, decoder-versus-detector comparison, capacity analysis and image case studies are retained. Appendix A.1 newly lists Figure 10, but that variability illustration already exists in v1.

E5.justification: Both report the same five-fold evaluation and mean/standard-error practice for FID and CLIP, and the same standard-error reporting for LPIPS across ten prompts. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all values, including PRC COCO FID 76.5979, SDP FID 63.7350 and LPIPS 0.7589. The plotted results, 512-bit robustness and 2500-bit capacity findings, and Appendix D VAE outcomes are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes the bound on the absolute distinguishing-probability difference from 1/2 + O(n^-c) to O(n^-c). This localized mathematical correction aligns the theorem with the existing pseudorandomness argument. The assumptions, remaining theorems and appendix proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of undetectability, quality preservation, robustness and long-message encoding. Theorem 1's correction formalizes the already-stated undetectability claim without changing these contribution claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of quality, variability and attack results remain unchanged. Both retain the practical-security qualifications in Section 3 and Appendix C.3, including the warning that experimental parameters do not guarantee undetectability against motivated adversaries.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, H100 hardware disclosure, attack configurations, PRC parameters and library information are unchanged. The code repository and data-access references remain the same; wrapping the abstract's repository URL introduces no access change.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior watermarking and PRC constructions are unchanged. v2 supplies a URL for the existing Biden executive-order reference, which is bibliographic completion rather than a new citation or positioning change.

P1.justification: v2 divides the abstract into two paragraphs, adds the omitted Figure 10 entry to Appendix A.1's overview, and completes a reference URL. The section sequence and scientific narrative remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–2 retain their contents and designs. Text reflow shifts Table 2 and surrounding material; notably, Theorem 2's inequalities become separated across pages 6–7 by Figure 1.

improvement.justification: Correcting Theorem 1 from a 1/2 + O(n^-c) probability-gap bound to O(n^-c) resolves a mismatch with the existing undetectability argument. The added Figure 10 overview entry also improves navigation. These limited accuracy and clarity gains outweigh the minor pagination regression that splits Theorem 2 around Figure 1.
